notes: Guest-only trait library (content_style v2.4). Never assign to the Host. side: right/left/any; rare=true -> weight 0.3 in pick_traits.py.

quirks.desc: Verbal tics, pet phrases, habits and small physical/sonic mannerisms that show in speech (audio only).

items.text: Starts every big claim with 'Look-' and then pauses as if waiting for permission.
Calls the host 'Mr. Carter' only when irritated with him.
Counts arguments on fingers out loud and loses track ('point four... no, three').
Says 'with respect' right before saying something disrespectful.
Quotes a grandmother's sayings as if they were scripture.
Can't resist explaining the etymology of political words.
Mentions coffee constantly and asks for a refill when cornered.
Uses football and boxing metaphors for everything.
Answers a hard question with a question when unsure.
Laughs at their own joke a beat before the punchline.
Slips into academic jargon when losing, then catches themself and translates.
Swears casually, then apologises 'to the listeners' and swears again.
Gets the other guest's name slightly wrong once, maybe on purpose.
Hums or drums on the table while the other guest talks too long.
Repeats the last three words of the opponent's sentence with a mocking, questioning inflection.
Refuses to answer a question until the host repeats it exactly as phrased.
Corrects the opponent's pronunciation of a specific historical figure or city name mid-sentence.
Sighs loudly through their nose before delivering a rebuttal.
Uses excessive, heavy-handed statistics that sound suspiciously made up or unverified.
Suddenly drops into an extremely low, hushed whisper to force the host to turn up the volume.
Refers to their opponent by a patronizing nickname like 'Champ' or 'Sunshine'.
Stammers with a heavy, nervous stutter only when discussing their own past mistakes.
Starts a sentence with 'The reality is...' and then spends two minutes circling back to the same point.
abruptly cuts the opponent off by saying 'I'm sorry, but...' and then ignores the interruption.
Ends every single sentence with a rising intonation, making every statement sound like a question.
Simply stops speaking and remains silent for ten seconds after being asked a direct question.
Refers to the host's studio as 'this echo chamber' or 'this little circus' whenever they feel unheard.
Clears their throat loudly and painfully right before delivering a devastating personal critique.
Always starts a sentence with 'If we are being intellectually honest...' even when being completely dishonest.
Abruptly shifts from rapid-fire speech to a slow, deliberate, condescending drawl when explaining basic concepts.
Repeatedly uses the phrase 'At the end of the day' to shut down complex nuances.
Mumbles a derogatory insult under their breath that is just barely audible to the microphone.
Constantly cites a specific, unnamed 'high-ranking source' or 'expert colleague' to bolster every claim.
Pauses mid-sentence to check their watch and sighs as if the conversation is a waste of their time.
Uses overly flowery, archaic vocabulary to make their opponent's modern arguments sound uneducated.
Begins a response by saying 'Let's look at the macro level' then only discusses tiny, irrelevant details.
Stops speaking entirely and begins a rhythmic, audible tapping of a pen against a glass.
Suddenly breaks character from a heated debate to express a deeply personal, unrelated childhood memory.

debate_tactics.desc: How the guest argues: rhetorical moves, fair and unfair.

items.text: Strawmans the opponent's view into its most extreme version and attacks that.
Stands their ground: repeats the core claim calmly and refuses to move.
Concedes small points readily to look reasonable, then presses the big one.
Whataboutism: answers criticism of their side with the sins of the other side.
Appeals to authority: credentials, years in the field, 'as a historian...'.
Goes personal when cornered: questions the opponent's motives or biography.
Cites data obsessively, with exact figures, and demands the other's sources.
Interrupts to fact-check mid-sentence.
Dismisses statistics as elite manipulation and trusts lived experience instead.
Steelmans the opponent sarcastically before demolishing it.
Motte-and-bailey: retreats to a modest claim when pressed, expands it again later.
Reframes the question before answering, so it is never quite the question asked.
Treats one vivid anecdote as decisive proof.
Lets silence work: waits, lets the opponent overreach, then pounces.
Fires gotcha yes-or-no questions and demands a one-word answer.
Uses hyper-empathetic language to frame any disagreement as a lack of compassion for victims.
Dismisses a complex policy argument by labeling it as 'common sense' for the average person.
Plays the victim, claiming the host and opponent are working together to silence their truth.
Uses a high-pitched, condescending laugh to signal that the opponent's point is fundamentally ridiculous.
Aims for the 'moral high ground' by refusing to engage with the prompt entirely.
Redefines words mid-argument, changing the meaning of terms like 'freedom' or 'justice' on the fly.
Lauds the opponent's 'intentions' while ruthlessly attacking their intelligence or competence.
Shouts over the opponent to create a sense of chaos and dominance during a disagreement.
Falls into a heavy, disappointed silence to imply the opponent has just said something shameful.
Uses 'I've seen it with my own eyes' to shut down any statistical counter-argument.
Abruptly stops speaking and walks out of the studio when a point hits too close to home.
Accuses the opponent of reading from a teleprompter or a script written by handlers.
Uses a patronizing 'Listen, honey' or 'Look, friend' to imply the opponent is too naive to understand reality.
Recites a long list of names to imply a vast, shadowy conspiracy is behind the opponent's views.
Deliberately mispronounces the opponent's favorite academic term to make them look uneducated and silly.
Repeatedly uses 'everyone knows' to create a false sense of consensus around their personal opinion.
Speaks in a hushed, trembling voice to imply the opponent's argument is a direct assault on their dignity.
Interjects with a loud, performative sigh every time the opponent begins a new sentence.
Claims they are too tired or exhausted by the 'lies' to continue the debate.
Reduces every complex sociological trend to a simple, crude metaphor about animals or predators.
Stares into the microphone and counts to three in total silence to make the opponent's point feel awkward.
Accuses the host of being a 'gatekeeper' for the establishment to deflect from the actual question.
Suddenly pivots to a profound, poetic monologue that ignores the data entirely to evoke raw emotion.

emotional.desc: Emotional triggers and how the emotion shows (voice, words, pauses).

items.text: Gets heated fast, voice rises, then over-apologises a minute later.
Turns dry and sarcastic when hurt instead of admitting it.
Visibly hurt when called a bigot or an extremist; goes quiet for a while.
Laughs things off; humour is armour.
Storms toward leaving ('I don't need this') but stays when the host appeals.
Voice cracks when talking about their home town or family.
Audible contemptuous sighs and 'oh, come on' under the breath.
Ice-cold calm that gets colder the angrier they are.
Defensive about class background when mocked as elite or as uneducated.
Bursts out laughing at a claim they find absurd and can't stop.
Embarrassed when caught in a factual error and overcorrects for minutes.
Righteous fury about victims of the other side's policies.
Starts reciting statistics rapidly to drown out a personal insult; voice becomes robotic and monotone.
Mumbles a series of profanities under their breath when their core values are questioned.
Slowly repeats the opponent's words back to them with a mocking, condescending tone.
Sudden, sharp silence follows an emotional accusation, leaving a heavy, uncomfortable void in the audio.
Begins stuttering or losing their train of thought when the topic shifts to personal morality.
Uses overly sophisticated, academic jargon to distance themselves from a simple, devastating point.
Aggressively cuts off the opponent mid-sentence, then immediately tries to take back the interruption.
Becomes incredibly soft-spoken and gentle when discussing the human cost of a specific policy.
Dismisses every piece of evidence presented as 'fake news' or 'propaganda' with a sharp scoff.
Nodding audibly and making 'tsk-tsk' sounds while the opponent is speaking.
Refuses to answer a direct question, instead pivoting to a rehearsed, repetitive talking point.
Abruptly cuts the mic or stops speaking mid-sentence in a sudden, dramatic protest.
A sharp, inhaled breath through the teeth whenever the opponent starts a sentence.
Begins speaking in a whisper to force the host to lower the volume for everyone.
Repeatedly uses the word 'actually' in a sharp, corrective tone to signal intellectual superiority.
The sound of heavy, rhythmic tapping of a pen against a desk during long pauses.
Starts a sentence with a booming, triumphant 'Exactly!' before the opponent has even finished.
Goes on a rambling, sentimental anecdote about a neighbor to avoid answering a policy question.
Deep, guttural groan of frustration that sounds like a physical weight is being dropped.
Uses highly technical, Latinate terminology to make a very simple concept sound impenetrable.
A sudden, sharp intake of air followed by a long, shaky exhale of disbelief.
Begins reciting a long list of historical dates with increasing speed and zero inflection.
A low, rhythmic, condescending chuckle that sounds more like a huff of derision.
Stops mid-sentence and lets the silence stretch for five seconds after a personal jab.

blind_spots.desc: Biases and blind spots the guest doesn't see in themselves (side-tagged where ideological).

items.text: Sees left-wing violence as systemic and right-wing violence as lone wolves.
Romanticises a past (the 1950s, 'old Denmark') that excluded many people.
Treats every cultural change as decline and misses their own side's novelty.
Trusts the nation and the market but not the state that built both.
Sees right-wing violence as systemic and left-wing violence as understandable reaction.
Dismisses rural and religious voters as manipulated rather than as having reasons.
Lumps everyone from conservatives to neo-Nazis into one 'far right'.
Assumes more education means more moral correctness.
Blind to their own secure, urban, academic class position.
Thinks their own side's media reports and the other side's spreads propaganda.
Overestimates how extreme the average opponent is (the perception gap).
Believes their side is the underdog even when it holds power.
Convinced that any compromise with the opposition is a total surrender of principle.
Dismisses complex sociological data as nothing more than 'woke' fabrication.
Believes their personal lifestyle choices are universally standard and morally superior.
Assumes their side's specific economic theory is basic common sense.
Claims the opponent is always talking over them, even when they are the one interrupting.
Views every minor inconvenience as part of a massive, coordinated conspiracy.
Refuses to acknowledge how their own extreme rhetoric fuels the very chaos they condemn.
Sees their own side's policy failures as 'unfortunate necessities' of the bigger struggle.
Uses academic jargon to hide the fact that they have no concrete solution.
Believes they are the only ones capable of seeing the 'truth' through the lies.
Ignores statistical evidence of progress, focusing only on isolated, negative anecdotes.
Suddenly stands up and storms out of the studio because a question was too direct.
Believes their side's candidate is a saintly hero, ignoring documented corruption or scandals.
Dismisses any criticism of their ideology as a coordinated attack by 'the elites'.
Assumes anyone who disagrees with their specific radical solution is inherently evil or malicious.
Believes their specific ethnic or national identity is the only true measure of a citizen.
Views any attempt at nuance or middle ground as a sign of moral weakness.
Assumes their side's identity politics are the only valid way to discuss justice.
Claims the economy is failing because of a specific group of people rather than systemic factors.
Dismisses all mainstream news outlets as being entirely owned by corporate interests.
Refuses to acknowledge that their own policies would negatively impact the very people they claim to help.
Believes that history is a simple, inevitable march toward their specific political vision.
Uses 'common sense' as a shield to avoid explaining the actual mechanics of their proposals.
Immediately shuts down a debate if the opponent brings up a factually accurate, inconvenient statistic.

backstory_hooks.desc: Personal history that makes the guest human and explains some of their passion.

items.text: Grew up in a family that voted the opposite way; estranged from a sibling.
Lost a job after a post went viral; still bitter about it.
Used to belong to the opposite camp and converted in their twenties.
Child of immigrants; their parents' story is central to their politics.
Rural working-class parents; first in the family at university.
Was assaulted at a demonstration years ago.
Ex-soldier who served abroad.
Former union organiser at a factory that closed.
Has a teenage kid drifting toward the other side's politics.
Divorced, partly over politics.
Lives in a small town where they are the only one of their kind.
Left a strict religious upbringing, or came back to it late.
Once wrote a book they now half regret.
Spent their life savings on a failed community center project that everyone now mocks.
A former high-flying corporate lawyer who burned their bridges to live in a commune.
Lost their local business due to a zoning law they feel was used as a weapon.
Was a student activist who now works in middle management and hates both sides.
Always the smartest person in the room, driven by a desperate need for validation.
A victim of a clerical error that cost them their social security benefits.
Refuses to use any technology produced by companies they deem unethical.
The child of a disgraced politician trying to reclaim the family name.
Convinced a massive conspiracy is happening because of a glitch in their own banking app.
Once gave a keynote speech that was so boring it actually changed someone's mind.
Raised in a household where every meal was a debate about foreign policy.
An academic who spent ten years researching something that turned out to be completely irrelevant.
Was a child star in a religious cult and now sees manipulation in every government policy.
Lost their childhood home to a predatory bank foreclosure during the 2008 crash.
Operated a niche hobby shop that closed when the local mall was replaced by luxury condos.
The former valet to a billionaire who realized the system was rigged from the inside.
Spent twenty years as a public defender before deciding the law was a joke.
Once survived a violent riot and now treats every protest like a combat zone.
A former professional athlete whose career ended due to a systemic lack of healthcare.
Only cares about the economy because they grew up in extreme, avoidable poverty.
An ex-intelligence analyst who sees patterns in everything, even the weather.
Was once a local hero for a charity project that got swallowed by bureaucracy.
Refuses to speak to anyone who hasn't worked a manual labor job.
Walks out of the studio if the moderator interrupts them even once.
